passages.note: Status page shows prime sponsorship and enactment but prints no operative provision.

passages.provision_quote: REQUIREMENTS FOR EXTRA HIGH LOAD FACTOR CUSTOMER PAYMENTS TO COVER THE COSTS OF ANY INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENTS, ADDITIONS OR expansions THAT ARE NECESSARY TO FACILITATE SERVICE TO THE CUSTOMER, WHICH SHALL BE SUPPORTED BY SCHEDULES that are FILED BY THE ELECTRIC PUBLIC SERVICE CORPORATION THAT DEMONSTRATE THE PROTECTION OF NON-extra HIGH LOAD FACTOR CUSTOMERS FROM subsidizing extra-high load factor customers.
passages.note: The text never names data centers and only authorizes ('MAY ... ESTABLISH') commission cost-allocation terms plus semiannual interconnection reports.
Divided House final reading (16 No of 60 voting), so not near-unanimous, but the page prints no provision.

rows.reasoning: Griffin prime-sponsored and voted Yes on HB2756 (2026), which requires semiannual reports on new extra high load factor customers and lets the corporation commission require those customers to pay infrastructure costs so that non-extra high load factor customers are protected from subsidizing them. That leans toward managing large-load costs and disclosure, but it does not bar utilities "from passing any data center energy infrastructure costs to residential customers", it imposes no "impact assessments, energy cost-sharing agreements, and community benefit requirements before approval", and it says nothing about "streamlined permitting" or "transparency about projected energy demand and rate impacts". No single rung is matched clause for clause, so the evidence separates the sides but not the rungs.
